hook.headline: A record is not deeply immutable
hook.hook: Record components cannot be reassigned after construction, but a component can still reference mutable state.
hook.visualCaption: Final component reference does not mean frozen object graph.

mentalModel.title: Fixed bindings, potentially mutable contents
mentalModel.coreIdea: A Java record gives final component fields, generated accessors, and value-oriented equality based on its components. It does not recursively freeze objects referenced by those components.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: Records are strong API boundary types when their components are themselves immutable or defensively copied where mutation would violate the contract.
mentalModel.mentalShortcut: record freezes references, not everything they reference

code.title: Defensively copy mutable input
code.intro: If the API contract requires stable tags, copy the incoming list in the compact constructor.
code.highlightReason: List.copyOf creates an unmodifiable snapshot of the supplied elements, so later structural changes to the source list do not change this record component.
code.takeaway: Use records for concise value carriers, but make mutability decisions explicit at collection and object boundaries.
code.professionalNote: List.copyOf is shallow: the list structure is unmodifiable, but mutable element objects can still change unless they are immutable or copied too.

production.title: Protect boundary contracts
production.scenario: A controller accepts a record DTO containing a mutable collection, then passes it into asynchronous or downstream processing.
problems: A shared collection can be mutated after record construction.
Logs, validation results, or downstream behavior can then observe state different from the state originally received.
production.professionalApproach: Decide whether each component is safe to share. Prefer immutable component types; defensively copy mutable collections when stable snapshot semantics matter. Keep this separate from Bean Validation, which checks constraints but does not make referenced objects immutable.
production.debugClue: If a record appears to change, inspect mutable components and aliases to their referenced objects before assuming record semantics changed.

interview.question: Are Java records immutable, and are they suitable for REST request or response DTOs?
interview.answer: Records have final component fields, so their component references cannot be reassigned after construction. That is shallow immutability, not deep immutability: a component may reference a mutable collection or object whose state can still change. Records are often a good DTO fit when value semantics and concise carriers are appropriate, but mutable inputs may need defensive copying and validation remains a separate concern.
remember: Referenced objects may still be mutable
